summary: H.R. 10912, the Fast Tracking European Investment in Ukraine's Defense Act, amends the Arms Export Control Act to pre-approve the transfer of specific U.S.-made defense articles from certain allied nations to the Government of Ukraine. The bill establishes a U.S. policy to welcome allied investment in the U.S. defense industrial base and facilitate increased contributions to Ukraine's defense while Russia's invasion continues.

affected_groups.effect: Can receive pre-approved third-party transfers of specific U.S.-made munitions from eligible allied nations, provided it commits in writing not to retransfer them without presidential consent and takes custody before the deadline.
Can transfer eligible U.S.-supplied defense articles they purchased to Ukraine with pre-approval, bypassing certain standard transfer restrictions.
affected_groups.group: Governments of NATO member countries, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Israel, and New Zealand

key_provisions: States U.S. policy to welcome long-term investment from allies in the U.S. defense industrial base and facilitate contributions to Ukraine's defense during Russia's invasion.
Pre-approves the transfer of specific defense articles sold by the U.S. to governments in NATO, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Israel, or New Zealand if transferred to Ukraine.
Limits eligible defense articles to 155mm artillery shells, 155mm Excalibur extended range artillery shells, HIMARS munitions, or GMLRS munitions.
Requires the Government of Ukraine to provide a written commitment not to transfer the items to any other foreign country or person without presidential consent.
Requires Ukraine to accept title and physical custody of the transferred defense articles before December 31, 2030, with possible annual extensions by the Secretary of State up to December 31, 2035.
Requires the President to promptly notify specified congressional leaders and committees before a transfer of defense articles is made.
missing_information: The bill does not specify funding amounts, cost estimates, or budget impacts.
The source material does not provide details on the volume or exact monetary value of the defense articles eligible for transfer.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10912, the Fast Tracking European Investment in Ukraine's Defense Act, amends the Arms Export Control Act to pre-approve the transfer of specific U.S.-made defense articles from certain allied nations to the Government of Ukraine. The bill establishes a U.S. policy to welcome allied investment in the U.S. defense industrial base and facilitate increased contributions to Ukraine's defense while Russia's invasion continues.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts how quickly and easily certain U.S.-made munitions can be transferred from specific international allies to Ukraine, streamlining approval processes under the Arms Export Control Act through December 31, 2030 (or up to 2035 if extended).
